# Instructions for Claude

## Generated files

`src/tokens.json` is the source of truth. `dist/` (except `dist/vue/`), `docs/reference.md` and
`demo/index.html` are generated by `scripts/build.mjs`; `dist/vue/` is built by Vite from
`src/vue/`. `npm run build` does both. Never hand-edit them: change the source or the build script, run
`npm run build`, then `npm test` (it fails if generated files are stale or a text colour drops below
4.5:1). Commit the source and the regenerated files together.

## Keep docs/ in sync

`docs/` holds the _why_, one file per area (tokens, theming, and later components). When a change
adds or alters how something works, update the matching `docs/*.md` in the same change. Use
concrete paths and real code, and flag footguns explicitly.

## Inline comments

Keep them short (about 5 lines at most): footguns ("change this and X breaks"), public API docs, or
a one-line pointer to `docs/<area>.md`. History and rationale go in `docs/`, not inline.

## Components

Read [docs/components.md](docs/components.md) before adding or changing one: one look per
component (chosen by christopher when projects disagree), styles in `@layer components` with `fu-`
classes and token values only, behaviour and server-render tests in `src/vue/components.spec.js`.
The stale-file test doesn't cover `dist/vue/`, so always rebuild before committing.

## Consumers

furioursus.dev (Astro + Tailwind v4), mtg-csv-sorter and mtg-library-value-tracker (static, no
build). Anything in `dist/` except `dist/vue/` must keep working from a plain `<link>`/`<script>`
with no bundler.

## Commits

Every commit is christopher's: author and committer `Christopher Kennedy-Nuñez <yo@git.furioursus.dev>`, never `yo@github.furioursus.dev` or a Claude address.

- No AI attribution: no `Co-Authored-By`, "Generated with" or session links. `.claude/settings.json` turns Claude Code's off, including in cloud sessions.
- Conventional Commits with a lowercase imperative subject. Add a body only when the why isn't obvious: one line per paragraph or bullet, never hard-wrapped, American spelling.
